FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A02
The examiner proceeds to evaluate safe driving only after the vehicle passes its inspection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A02
Dangerous driving, a law violation, a crash, failure to follow examiner instructions or too many driving errors can cause road-test failure. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A02
The examiner may ask the applicant to demonstrate vehicle controls before the road test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A02
A control demonstration may include the horn, parking lights, high and low beams, turn signals, wipers, parking brake, hazard flashers and defroster. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A02
Incorrect operation of any vehicle control causes road-test failure. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A02
The parallel-parking task uses a space 24 feet long and eight feet wide between two uprights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A02
During the parking task, position the vehicle midway between the uprights with the entire vehicle within the space. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A02
The parking task prohibits touching either upright, crossing the painted boundary or driving onto or over the curb. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A02
The applicant has one parallel-parking attempt and may make no more than three adjustments. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A02
A vehicle with a self-parking system may be used for testing only while that feature is switched off and remains unused throughout the road test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A02
The examiner is the only passenger permitted during the road test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A02
At the start of the road test, the examiner tells the applicant the route and required maneuvers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A02
The examiner observes compliance with warning signs, stop signs and traffic lights during the driving test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A02
Vehicle control and use of turn signals to communicate with other drivers are evaluated during the road test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A02
An applicant passing the road test at a PennDOT Driver License Center receives the driver license at that time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A02
A driver younger than 18 who fails the road test must wait seven days before retesting. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R17 | anchor: A02
Each learner permit allows three road-test attempts before the permit expires. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R18 | anchor: A02
After a third road-test failure, the applicant must reapply to extend the learner permit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R19 | anchor: A02
Three failed road-test attempts or permit expiration can be addressed by obtaining DL-31 for the non-commercial learner permit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R20 | anchor: A02
If the road test has not been taken or passed within three years after the physical examination, the applicant must file a new DL-180 application and retake the knowledge test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-R21 | anchor: A02
Not using turn signals is among the listed reasons for road-test failure. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]
